# kodawari

> kodawari is a command-line tool that turns a written feature spec into
> finished, tested code. You give it a markdown file describing a feature; it
> plans the work, writes the code into your project, runs your tests for real,
> has a second AI model review and auto-fix the result, and hands you a
> ready-to-ship feature to approve — like a small autonomous engineering team
> (planner, reviewer, executor) that works from a spec instead of a chat.

It coordinates three independent LLM roles — a planner, a reviewer, and an
executor — and is a headless, contract-first alternative to interactive
AI pair-programmers like Claude Code, Cursor, Aider, and OpenHands. The three
LLM roles are configured independently, so you can mix providers (GPT, Claude,
Gemini, local models). Greenfield is first-class: an empty directory plus a PRD
produces a scaffolded, tested feature. Every stage writes a JSON-schema-validated
artifact, and under `KODAWARI_REVIEW_ENABLED=1` silent-pass fallback paths fail
closed. Python 3.11+, MIT licensed, public beta (v0.1.2).
